data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 (Volume IV) factsheet summarizes Costa Rica’s performance in the financial literacy assessment, which was administered for the fourth time in PISA (2012, 2015, 2018, 2022). Financial literacy was assessed via a computer-based test with multiple-choice and constructed-response items organized around real-life passages; students in sampled schools were split so that one group took financial literacy plus either mathematics or reading, while the other took the core PISA subjects (mathematics, reading, science). In Costa Rica, 3,279 students participated in the financial literacy assessment, representing 53,068 15-year-olds. The factsheet reports an average score of 418 (below the OECD average), with 43% below Level 2 and about 1% at Level 5. It also provides descriptive associations between financial literacy and mathematics/reading performance and highlights differences by gender and immigrant background, plus self-reported financial behaviors and school exposure to financial concepts. Methodological details on plausible-value combining and missing-data handling are not provided in the excerpt.
